add.title: Transgender rights in Texas (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Wikipedia state-rights article (accessed 4 Oct 2026): Governor Abbott signed the Women's Privacy Act on 22 September 2025; it requires bathrooms matching the sex on one's birth certificate and explicitly applies to public schools, universities, prisons and Texas government buildings, with $25,000 (first) / $125,000 (subsequent) facility fines, effective 4 December 2025. Documents that Texas' most recent gender-placements statute reaches prisons — but on restroom use, not on cell/facility assignment or trans-prisoner housing placement.

add.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia) — Gibson v. Collier (2019) ruling
add.summary: Wikipedia article on LGBTQ prisoners (accessed 4 Oct 2026), Gibson v. Collier section: Vanessa Lynn Gibson, a transgender woman incarcerated in Texas by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice and diagnosed with gender dysphoria, was denied gender-confirmation surgery because TDCJ's official treatment policy excluded GCS. The federal district court denied the state's immunity defences but ruled against her on the Eighth Amendment claim; the Fifth Circuit affirmed dismissal (no deliberate indifference; refusing GCS is a permissible medical choice under Kosilek), with Judge Barksdale dissenting on summary-judgement procedure.
